name: The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach
positioning: Oceanfront Ritz-Carlton on Lincoln Road in Miami Beach's Art Deco Historic District, a Morris Lapidus building that opened in 1953 as The DiLido Hotel, with José Andrés Group dining
best_for: Travelers who want oceanfront dining and a beach bar from José Andrés Group
Families with children aged 5 to 11 who want Ritz Kids programming

facts.text: The hotel is on Lincoln Road in the heart of the Art Deco Historic District.
Zaytinya is a mezze-style restaurant drawing on Turkish, Greek and Lebanese cuisines.
Lapidus Bar pays tribute to architect Morris Lapidus with bronze accents, craft cocktails and live music.
The spa has 11 treatment rooms, a co-ed relaxation lounge, separate male and female lounges, and steam and sauna facilities.
Daily beachfront fitness classes are led by local instructors.
Rooms have marble bathrooms with Diptyque amenities, and select rooms and suites have private balconies or poolside patios.
Ocean-view rooms and suites make up a majority of the room categories.
Ritz Kids offers daily programming for children ages 5-11, including beachfront activities.
Guests can craft a personalized 55 ml fragrance with a Miami fragrance expert.

highlights.text: The hotel was designed by architect Morris Lapidus and opened as The DiLido Hotel in 1953.
Dining is by José Andrés Group at three venues: Zaytinya, Lapidus Bar and DiLido Beach Bar.
The Ritz-Carlton Club presents complimentary culinary offerings five times a day, prepared by José Andrés Group, for Club guests.
A private airboat experience in the Everglades, with private transportation and a narrated scenic drive, is offered as a curated adventure.
DiLido Beach Bar offers Atlantic views and direct beach access.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service.
Club access requires a confirmed Club-level reservation, and Marriott Bonvoy Elite Status does not include complimentary Club Lounge access.
WhataHotel notes the high-energy South Beach location may not suit all travelers.
